A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShortV study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. The appendices are retained but moved after the references in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original layer-contribution measurements, benchmark evaluations, latency measurements, ablations, and qualitative ShortV outputs, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports FastV and VTW results on Flickr30K.

M1.justification: Sections 2-3 retain the same LC-based layer selection and training-free freezing of visual-token updates. The sparse layer architecture, parameter N, and compatibility with FastV are unchanged.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets and tasks are unchanged. Although Flickr30K appears in Table 1 for the first time in v2, v1 already evaluates captioning on this dataset in Tables 2 and 11. The appendix scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds FastV and VTW as comparators on Flickr30K in Table 1; v1 reports Flickr30K results only for vanilla models and ShortV configurations in Tables 2 and 11. Comparator membership in the other evaluations and ablations is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, baseline parameters, calibration design, FLOPs assumptions, and MMMU first-token latency protocol are unchanged. The added Flickr30K entries use the existing CIDEr metric. Removing the A100 specification changes hardware disclosure without establishing an actual experimental-setting change.

E4.justification: The efficiency sweeps, FastV combination experiment, layer-selection and frozen-token ablations, and Appendix C qualitative cases are unchanged, including their results in Tables 2 and 5-11.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds eight Flickr30K CIDEr results for FastV/VTW: 67.5/44.5 on LLaVA-1.5-7B, 73.4/65.9 on LLaVA-1.5-13B, 66.7/38.4 on LLaVA-NeXT-7B, and 66.0/56.6 on LLaVA-NeXT-13B. The accompanying vanilla/ShortV values repeat v1 Tables 2 and 11. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The LC definition and computational-cost equations in Sections 2.2 and 3.2, including Equations 1-5, are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim substantial visual-token layer redundancy, introduce LC and ShortV, and claim approximately 60% of layers can freeze visual tokens while preserving performance. The abstract's 50% FLOPs reduction example and the conclusion retain the same scope.

C2.justification: The modality-gap explanation, discussion of alternative layer-importance metrics, and interpretations of efficiency and ablation results are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning coarse layer granularity and possible token-update refinements.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code release from promised to reported public availability at the same repository. Conversely, Tables 3 and 4 remove the A100 specification and state only 'single GPU.' Appendix B's calibration sample counts and selected layer IDs are retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 57 works and retain the same research positioning, including relationships to ShortGPT, SAISA, and token-pruning methods. Reference relocation and updated page backreferences do not change the cited research.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author indicators, shortens the institutional affiliation, removes appendix pointers from Sections 4.2-4.3, and places the appendices after the references. The scientific narrative otherwise remains substantially verbatim.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a Flickr30K CIDEr column and becomes wider. Tables 3-4 have edited captions, and the acknowledgments and appendix relocation cause limited layout changes. Existing figures and appendix displays are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added Flickr30K baselines fill a small comparison gap, revealing both ShortV's strengths and FastV's higher score on LLaVA-NeXT-7B (66.7 versus 65.7 CIDEr). V2 also reports code availability. These modest gains outweigh the loss of GPU specificity and appendix pointers, while the central method and conclusions remain unchanged.
